rationale: Total refracting power of the eye is a high-yield recall fact; cornea vs lens contribution is a classic viva trap
Bitemporal hemianopia from chiasmal lesions vs homonymous hemianopia is the key lesion-localisation discriminator students must internalise
Correcting lens type is a fundamental discriminator; students often confuse concave/convex for myopia vs hypermetropia
Presbyopia and accommodation are commonly misunderstood; students must know that the mechanism is lens sclerosis, not ciliary muscle weakness
The pinhole test principle — eliminating peripheral aberrations to isolate refractive vs non-refractive causes of blurred vision — is a key clinical discriminator
6/6 is not 'perfect' vision — it is merely the minimum passing standard; students must understand the Snellen notation correctly to avoid clinical underestimation
Keratoconus is the absolute contraindication to corneal laser surgery — the single highest-stakes screening question in refractive surgery counselling
Students commonly believe LASIK can correct any degree of myopia; residual corneal thickness limit is a key safety constraint they must know
Distinguishing strabismic from anisometropic amblyopia is clinically important because the former is usually unilateral with a deviating eye, while the latter may be invisible without measurement
The critical period cutoff for amblyopia treatment is a key examiner trap — patching after the critical period has very limited benefit
